title: Doctrine of the Trinity
short_answer: The Trinity teaches that one God exists eternally as three Persons: Father, Son, and Holy Spirit.
summary: There is one God who eternally exists in three distinct Persons: Father, Son, and Holy Spirit. Each Person is fully God, yet there is one God.
explanation: The Trinity teaches that there is only one God in essence, yet three distinct Persons: the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit. The Father is not the Son, the Son is not the Spirit, and the Spirit is not the Father. Yet each Person is fully God. This doctrine is revealed throughout Scripture and affirmed by the early church.
historical_context: The doctrine was clarified in the early Church to defend the full deity of Christ and the Holy Spirit against heresies.
major_points: The Trinity revealed progressively in Scripture
common_questions: Is the Trinity in the Bible?
Why do Christians believe in the Trinity?
